patches: P2 (grammar.js): `∞` is a real Julia UNARY operator — `∞(x)` and `x + ∞` both parse — and it was absent from `OPERATORS.unary`, so every use became an ERROR node. 7 of the 185 defect files.

P3 (grammar.js): `const global x = 1` is valid Julia and is how Base declares a global constant (`const global maxprobeshift = 6` in base/dict.jl). The rule read `const` then an assignment, so `global` had nowhere to go; the fix is `optional('global')`, which needs a declared conflict against the existing `global_statement` because both forms are valid. 10 of the 185 defect files.

P4 (grammar.js): an abstract type may carry a BODY and may put it on one line — `abstract type Inserter; end` in Compiler/src/ssair/ir.jl. The rule went from `type_head` straight to `end`; the fix mirrors `struct_definition`, which sits three rules below already doing the right thing, so the correct shape was available in the file and this rule simply omitted it. 5 of the 185 defect files.

P5 (grammar.js): a function can be NAMED by an operator, and the language's own libraries do it — `function ⊑ end` in Compiler/src/abstractlattice.jl declares the abstract-lattice ordering relation, and `function ⊇ end` appears in base/abstractset.jl. `signature` offered an identifier, a call, an argument list, a typed expression and a where-expression, none of which can BE `⊑`; the fix reuses the existing public `operator` rule rather than adding a second spelling. 46 of the 185 defect files — the second-largest class.

P1 IS DELIBERATELY NOT LANDED: `+%` and `-%` are Julia's wrapping add and subtract (52 of the 185 defect files) and Julia lexes an operator as a maximal run of operator characters, so `+%` is ONE operator name. Three variants were MEASURED and all three are recorded in PIN.md. `-%` collides with `-=` and `+%` with `+`, both two characters, so precedence decides — and tree-sitter's lexer stops at the first accepting state, so a wrapping token that outranks `+` is never read. Over the corpus: the `times` variant fixed 24 and broke 3; `prec(-1)` fixed 9 and broke 1; the third fixed 0 and broke 0. A real fix needs a lexer-level change (an external scanner emitting the operator run, which is what Julia's own lexer does), which belongs upstream rather than in a vendored copy.
provenance.patchEvidence: Behavioural A/B against an INDEPENDENT oracle — Julia 1.11.3's own parser via `Meta.parseall`, which shares no code, no grammar and no data model with tree-sitter — over 949 corpus files, re-runnable via `bun run script/m12/julia-differential.ts [--wasm=<alt>]` (artifact: validation/m12/results/julia-differential.json). Baseline: pristine 0.23.1 rejects 185 files Julia accepts, with 0 in the other direction. PATCHED vs PRISTINE: fixes 9, breaks 1, 177 error files remaining. The single break is base/Enums.jl (0 -> 6 ERROR nodes) at a one-line `primitive type $(esc(typename)) <: Enum{...} end` inside a `Base.@__doc__(...)` macro call — NOT reproducible by any of five minimal probes of that shape, so it is a file-scale parse shift, and it is recorded rather than hidden. WIRED vs a REBUILD of this committed patched source: 0 fixed, 0 broken, 949 unchanged — the bytes differ by 3 (5,892,544 vs 5,892,547) as wasm builds must, so identity is claimed on behaviour. The oracle uses `parseall` and NOT `parse` because Julia's `parse` resolves operators in a single-expression scope and REJECTS `a +% b`, which `parseall` accepts: an oracle on `parse` would report the language's own wrapping-add operator as invalid. The harness also refuses to report a verdict without counting the oracle's own coverage, because the first version 'agreed' on 949 files while the oracle had returned nothing at all.

julia.decision: Pin as a LOCAL REBUILD OF THE PATCHED VENDORED SOURCE, and the reason is a change of kind that had to be recorded rather than assumed. This lane began byte-identical to the npm tarball — the strongest provenance in the registry — and the corpus differential ended that: 185 files of valid Julia that the grammar could not read, five named constructs, four patched. The kind follows the bytes, so it is now a rebuild, and the pin has to say so or the record is false. The question the C lane's own record had to answer first is the same one here: are the WIRED bytes a build of the PATCHED source? Measured answer: yes, behaviourally identical on all 949 routed files (0 fixed, 0 broken, 949 unchanged), with the 3-byte difference that two correct builds of one wasm source must show. The consequence is the useful one: the incumbent is a verified build, so no Julia measurement needs re-baselining, and had the wired bytes matched pristine the four patches would not have been live. This lane also retires a hazard this repo has paid for twice before. Every existing lane was written first and measured afterwards, and the measurement is what found the defects: Objective-C was CLOSED over an instrument reading 7 of 329 files, whose `grammarErrorFiles: 0` was 49 crashes counted as 49 clean parses. Julia is the lane where the order was reversed — the grammar census and the Julia-1.11.3 differential were built BEFORE any analyzer existed, precisely so that the analyzer would be written against a measured grammar instead of inheriting its 185 defects and then debugging itself for a day.

alternatives.option: Adopt npm tree-sitter-julia@0.23.1's own published wasm as the wired bytes
alternatives.measured: REJECTED, and this is the load-bearing measurement of the lane: it DELETES capability. Over 949 corpus files pristine rejects 185 that Julia accepts — 19.5% of the corpus — and the four patches remove 8 of those net. Concretely it loses the wrapping-add and subtract operators `+%`/`-%` (52 files), operator-named function definitions such as `function ⊑ end` and `function ⊇ end` (46 files), `const global` (10), the `∞` unary operator (7) and one-line `abstract type X; end` (5).

alternatives.option: Land P1 (`+%`/`-%`) with a lexical precedence and take the regression
alternatives.measured: REJECTED, and the reason is a lexer fact rather than a judgement about value. Three variants were built and measured over the whole corpus: placing the wrapping operators in the `times` class fixed 24 files and BROKE 3 (`base/special/pow.jl` and `base/twiceprecision.jl` lose `xu -%= (UInt64(52) << 52)`, base/Enums.jl loses 6 nodes); `token(prec(-1, ...))` fixed 9 and broke 1; `prec(1)` with the assignment operators raised to `prec(2)` fixed 0 and broke 0. The mechanism is that `-%` collides with `-=` and `+%` with `+`, both two characters, so precedence decides — and tree-sitter's lexer STOPS AT THE FIRST ACCEPTING STATE, so any wrapping token that outranks `+` is never read at all. A patch that fixes 24 and breaks 3 is not a patch to land; a real fix is lexical.

patches: P1 (#743, grammar.js): `macro_prefixed_objc_declaration` — a bare macro line above an @interface/@implementation/@protocol is a file-scope macro, not a declaration, and upstream reads it as a lone specifier closed by a MISSING `;`. Carries `prec(-1)`, which is load-bearing: raising it demands arbitration (`type_specifier, macro_prefixed_objc_declaration`), the wall the cpp half hit.

P2 (#743 follow-up, grammar.js): the same rule admitted in `_block_item` as well as `_top_level_item`, and this is the defect that made P1 useless in practice. tree-sitter-c builds a file-scope `preproc_if` body from `_block_item`, NOT `_top_level_item`, so registering P1 in `_top_level_item` alone made it UNREACHABLE inside every conditional. sdwebimage wraps most of its headers in `#if SD_UIKIT || SD_MAC`, so the fallthrough was the norm, and the ERROR node it produced ran 101 lines to the next `@end` — deleting a whole class and replacing its properties with phantoms named after the property ATTRIBUTES (`variable:strong`, `variable:copy`, `variable:assign`, `variable:readonly`) while reporting `properties: 0`.

P3 (M60, grammar.js): `macro_enum_specifier` for `typedef NS_ENUM(Underlying, Name) { ... };`, Apple's universal enum idiom, where the name is inside the macro's arguments and there is NO trailing declarator. Upstream collapses the body into ERROR nodes: 35 declarations, 164 named constants, 152 invisible (7.3% recovery) over the router's 329-file universe. Two properties are load-bearing and both measured. `prec(1)`, not `prec(-1)`: at -1 the rule generates, builds a wasm, and does NOTHING, because `NS_ENUM` is absorbed as a `type_identifier` and `(...)` as a `parenthesized_declarator` by default — a rule that never fires still passes a diff of the grammar file. And deliberately GENERIC (identifier, parenthesised args, brace body) rather than an NS_ENUM|NS_OPTIONS name list, because naming the five macros one corpus happened to use repeats a mistake this project already made in the yaml analyzer's include tags: a closed set built from the constructs someone thought to ask about. Aliased to `enum_specifier` at every admission point so the analyzer's existing C-enum path applies unchanged — which is also why it is a RULE and not a node type.

P4 (M60, grammar.js): `availability_macro_specifier` for Apple's trailing availability annotations, which are macro CALLS with nested parens, commas and string literals (`API_DEPRECATED_WITH_REPLACEMENT("use removeImageForKey:", macos(10.10, X), ios(8.0, X), ...)`). C's `macro_type_specifier` covers `MACRO(type)` — one type argument — and `attribute_specifier` covers `[[...]]`, so neither reached the shape; the annotation trails the last method parameter, the parse cannot continue, and the ERROR node swallows the ENCLOSING @protocol (83 lines; SDImageCacheDefine.h analysed to 0 methods where it has 7). Admitted ONLY via a local `_method_trailing_modifiers` and inside the method selector/parameter loop, and that narrowness is a measurement: admitting it through the shared `_declaration_modifiers` — the right-looking move, since the annotation really does trail a declaration — generated, built, and PASSED its minimal case, then took the corpus from 285 to 14,710 ERROR nodes and dropped 17,642 relationships across 239 of 329 files, because that hidden rule sits in every declaration and parameter position in the grammar and a rule whose arguments include a bare `identifier` outranks ordinary declarations almost everywhere (`UIApplicationMain(argc, argv)` in `main.m` was read as an annotation). Admitting it inside the loop is not optional: the loop offers only another selector or another parameter, and a trailing `AF_API_UNAVAILABLE(macos);` begins with an identifier, so `method_selector` claimed it and the method was published as `setDidFinishEventsForBackgroundURLSessionBlock:AF_API_UNAVAILABLE` — a selector IS identity in Objective-C, so that is a method that does not exist, carrying a `contains` row a consumer would route calls to, while the real selector is the one that vanishes.

objective-c.decision: Pin as a LOCAL REBUILD OF THE PATCHED VENDORED SOURCE, and the reason is that the prior question had to be answered before provenance could be stated at all. Most lanes in this file pin bytes byte-identical to a published package; that kind was unavailable here, because `wasm/tree-sitter-objc.wasm` (5,625,076 B, sha256 39799d7f...) is a rebuild of a patched source and npm's own tree-sitter-objc@3.0.2 wasm is 5,317,155 B. So the real question is whether the WIRED bytes are a build of the PATCHED source or a pristine build predating the patches, and it decides what every measurement in this lane means: the 9-fixture suite, the 5 grammar-wave mutants, the 329-file census, the 622-vs-158 error comparison and the enum-recovery number are all measurements of a parse produced by these bytes. Measured answer: the patches ARE live and the bytes ARE honest — a rebuild of the committed patched source is surface-identical to WIRED in both directions and analyzer-identical on all 329 routed files, while pristine differs by exactly the 8 node types the patches add and is worse on the corpus by 464 ERROR nodes, 316 symbols and 472 relationships. The consequence is the useful one: the incumbent was already a verified build, so no Objective-C measurement needs re-baselining, and had the wired bytes matched pristine, P1–P4 would not have been live and the whole lane would have needed re-measuring. This also retires a hazard that was carried for the entire #743 wave: objective-c was one of 21 lanes in the repository with a PATCHED, in-tree grammar and NO pin at all, which is the worst case for a pin rather than a mild one — the pin exists to catch 'the wired bytes are not a build of the source we think they are', and a patched grammar is exactly where that happens, because someone edits grammar.js, rebuilds, and every downstream number moves with no gate objecting.

The C rule it ports uses the FULL type_specifier, and that breadth does not port: in cpp `_scope_resolution` has an OPTIONAL scope, so `A::B` reads as either the qualified type `A::B` or macro `A` decorating `::B`. FIX 2 negative field numbers — `field_number` was a bare `int_lit` with no sign. The specification's field-number space is the signed 32-bit range with 19000-19999 reserved, so negative numbers are legal and occur in migrated schemas. FIX 3 `import option "...";` — editions' option-import, the mechanism behind `features`. Upstream's `import` allowed only `weak`/`public`. This was most of `descriptor.proto`'s damage.

A processing instruction with content therefore produced no `_pi_content` token, `<?target content?>` could not complete, and the parser wrapped the whole `<?...?>` in an ERROR node. It was not merely a lost declaration: with no XMLDecl present the enclosing `prolog` node disappeared too, taking any DOCTYPE in the same prolog with it. A 19-shape battery isolates it exactly: the construct parses iff the byte after `?>` is `\n` (fixtures/xml/out/pi-rootcause.json). `check_word` and `scan_comment` keep `advance_if_eq`, where a mismatch correctly means "not the token I was asked for".

patches: G5a/b: PowerShell 7 null-coalescing `??` and ternary `? :`, as two HIDDEN precedence levels
G5c: PowerShell 7 null-conditional `?.` and `?[`, added inside the rules that already define `.` and `[` so they inherit their associativity and precedence
G1: a script-level `param()` block after any other statement, reached through a statement-level form that deliberately omits the `attribute_list` and is ALIASED back to the `param_block` node name

G6: a command argument list whose values include a BARE WORD — one alternative whose elements are `generic_token`, which is DISJOINT from `array_literal_expression` (whose elements are `unary_expression`) by the deciding token, so it cannot consume a comma that rule owns

G7: a command ARGUMENT that is a sigil-led path (`$PSScriptRoot/x`, `$env:TEMP\a.txt`), a new token declared ONLY inside `_command_argument` so the state-driven lexer cannot produce it in the assignment right-hand side where `$a/$b` is division and must stay so

G8: `+` as .NET's nested-type separator in `type_name` (mirroring the `.` arm that already exists for the same reason), and `=` admitted to the DOUBLE-DASH branch of `command_parameter` only, because `--flag=value` is one argv token for a native command while PowerShell's own `-Name=value` is not valid

G9: a generic TYPE ARGUMENT may be a bracketed type (`Dictionary[[string],[int]]`), because `generic_type_arguments` could only take a `type_spec` and a `type_spec` can only express the SUFFIX array form `string[]` — the leading `[` of a `type_literal` had no route, so the derivation did not exist and the parser reached for the only one it had and failed

G10: a value GLUED to a double-dash parameter (--flag=..., --flag=$var), added as a PARSER alternative on the existing `command_parameter` and deliberately NOT as a second token — the third design, after two rejections whose causes are recorded in the decision

powershell.decision: Pin the patched local rebuild, and record both decisions that got here, because both were measured and one of them was a correction. (1) The BASE was identified by fetching all four published versions and hash-matching: the wired bytes were tree-sitter-powershell@0.25.10 (sha 1d30b5a2…, 983,236 B), not the 0.26.4 sitting in the npm cache. The only thing that said so was the full id enumeration — 415 ids vs 419, id-order digests differing, and a source diff naming `_string_literal_immediate`, the here-string fix. The NAMED vocabularies are identical (152), so a pin comparing named types alone would have passed two revisions as one, and the first grammar hunk would have been written against a grammar the product does not load. (2) The 0.25.10 → 0.26.4 upgrade was measured before it was taken: 0 files fixed, 0 broken over 73 production corpus files, identical 152 named types and 14 fields, 2 fewer ERROR nodes in ansible. (3) The PATCH is G5, and its provenance is stronger than any other lane's because the base was PROVEN before it was patched: the unpatched 0.26.4 source rebuilds to the published prebuild BYTE-FOR-BYTE (same 1,088,467 B, same sha), so the patch is a delta against a known artifact rather than against whatever the source happened to be. A rebuild's sha is not a function of its source across toolchain versions (M49 W19), so the patch's own sha is a local build and the ID-ORDER digest is the part that can be required to match — 419 ids / ff141f18453a becomes 423 ids / 50274a750a87 with G5a/b and 425 ids / 2edf2378eb2c with G5c, and the 152 NAMED types are unchanged at every step, which is the property that keeps an analyzer written against the old shapes from being silently re-pointed. (4) BOTH patches are strictly additive to the rules they extend. G5a/b inserts two hidden precedence levels and edits no existing rule. G5c adds one `choice` arm to `member_access`, one to `element_access` and one to `invokation_expression`, changing no precedence number and no existing arm; the operators are `token.immediate` for the same reason the `.` in `member_access` is, so `?.` is not recognised across whitespace and `$c ? .5 : 1.5` cannot be stolen. The one form whose meaning changes is `$c?[1,2] : $y` written tight, which this grammar now reads as null-conditional indexing — which is what PowerShell itself does, so the ambiguity is resolved the way the language resolves it rather than invented here. (5) G1 is the largest of the lane's grammar classes and the only one whose fix NECESSARILY changes a clean file's tree. A script's `param` block must be its first STATEMENT, but `using` statements may precede it, and a .psm1 module is REQUIRED to declare `using module` when it needs types — so `using` + `param(…)` is the ordinary shape for any parameterised script that uses a type. Under the pinned grammar `param($Name)` after a `using` line is not a `param_block` at all but a `command` named `param` whose argument is a parenthesized expression, so the parameter is never declared. The dangerous part is that this class is INVISIBLE to hasError-keyed gates: measured over the repro battery, 7 of 8 cases lose every parameter and 6 of those 7 report hasError=FALSE with zero ERROR and zero MISSING nodes, so F1, F10 and the M12 ERROR-node census all read them clean. 33 corpus files carry the shape (16 powershell, 17 ansible), and the ansible side went from 98 ERROR / 23 MISSING to 35 / 2 with 17 more symbols declared. The patch is one statement alternative, and two alternatives were measured and rejected first. (a) Deleting `program`'s own `optional($.param_block)` and keeping only the statement form would have re-shaped 11 of 35 clean powershell files and 2 of 9 clean ansible files — ~30% of the clean corpus — which F11's G2 gate fails on. (b) Putting `param_block` itself into the statement set fixed all 8 cases and silently REGRESSED a different construct: at statement position a leading `[` then had two uses, and the deterministic resolution took the param-block one, so `[ValidateSet('a','b')]$mode = 'a'` stopped being one pipeline and became an ERROR holding the attribute plus a detached pipeline holding the assignment. It surfaced as a fixture failure, not a corpus number. tree-sitter reported a `[param_block, _statement]` conflict declaration UNNECESSARY on both attempts — the automaton separates those routes on the text, so it can choose, and it chooses wrong; the fix had to remove the competing route rather than reprioritise it, hence the attribute-less `_bare_param_block` ALIASED back to `param_block` so the analyzer's existing `case "param_block"` and its descendant-walk lookup both work and the grammar's 152 named types do not grow. The cost of dropping the attribute from the statement form was measured, not assumed: 16 powershell and 17 ansible files have `using` followed by a BARE `param(`, and ZERO have `using` followed by an ATTRIBUTED one, while an attributed `param` block that IS the first statement still parses through the pre-existing program-level rule. What F11 says, and what was done about it: G1 damage passes (135 → 135 files, sites 891 → 882, 0 newly damaged) and G3 output is PERFECT (+1 pair, 0 lost, 0 symbols vanished, 0 re-attributed). G2 identity FAILS on exactly 11 files, and that failure is the cost of the fix rather than damage from it — those 11 are the files whose leading `param` block re-parents from `program` into `statement_list`, and G3 reports that NOT ONE of the 11 changed analyzer output at all. The analyzer is parent-agnostic by construction: it finds `param_block` with `collectChildrenByType`, a descendant walk, and already handles a `param_block` nested under a `script_block`. A tree-shape change the product does not consume is a different claim from one that does not matter, and it is the claim the evidence supports. Two attempts to suppress the 11 with dynamic precedence are recorded in the grammar and both failed — `prec.dynamic(1)` on `program` is inert because `program` is the parent of both parses, and `prec.dynamic(-1)` on the statement route does not change the outcome while re-breaking the attribute-attach shape. (6) G6 is the largest class in the lane and the one whose SHAPE was decided by measurement rather than by taste. In the pinned grammar a comma-separated command argument list works for every value kind EXCEPT a bare word: `'deb', 'rpm'` parses, `$a, $b` parses, `(1), (2)` parses, `1, 2` parses, and `deb, rpm` is 2 ERROR nodes. The reason is that `array_literal_expression` is `prec.left(seq($.unary_expression, repeat(seq(',', $.unary_expression))))` and a bare word is not reachable as a `unary_expression` — so the one value kind that matters most in command position, where an unquoted word is a command name or a bare argument, is the one that cannot form a list. Measured footprint: 245 parameter-form sites across both production corpora plus 2 module-surface bare sites, of which 8 are the `Export-ModuleMember` lines this lane's own `exports` reader is built to read. The first attempt at the patch was a bare `seq(',', tail)` among the `_command_element` alternatives. It scored 135 -> 107 damaged files, MISSING 139 -> 81, +253 pairs with 0 lost and 7 corpus files fixed — and was still wrong, because it stole the comma from INSIDE `array_literal_expression`: a two-element array became a one-element array plus an orphaned literal. G1 could not see it (error count 0 before and 0 after), the analyzer could not see it (byte-identical output on all 34 affected files), and `prec(-1)` on the comma element did not help because it was never a precedence tie. The admitted form is one alternative whose list elements are `generic_token`, which makes it disjoint from the array rule on the FIRST TOKEN of each element rather than merely lower-precedence than it. On the corpus: F11 G1 135 -> 110 damaged files with MISSING 139 -> 81, G2 identity 265 clean files with 0 tree differences, G3 +252 pairs with 0 lost and 0 symbols vanished — ADMISSIBLE — and the same 7 production files fixed with 0 broken that the rejected form fixed, without the shape change. The repro battery's named limits go 9 -> 7. (7) G7 is the LARGEST class in the lane — 1,002 sites in 155 files in `powershell` and 81 in 15 in `ansible`, 1,083 in 170 files — and the deciding token is an asymmetry inside one character class. `generic_token` is `token(/[^\(\)\$"'\-\{\}@\|\[\`\&\s][^\&\s\(\)\}\|;,]*/)`: the CONTINUATION class allows `/` and `\`, but the FIRST-character class excludes `$`. So `a/b` lexes as one token and `$a/b` cannot, and in PowerShell `$PSScriptRoot/x` is a single path argument. The battery had named this class `backslash-path`, which is wrong — `\` and `/` fail identically and `Import-Module $PSScriptRoot` alone parses clean — and two of the battery's own controls were themselves broken, which is why the class was mis-named in the first place. The patch is a new token declared ONLY inside `_command_argument`. That scoping is the whole safety argument and it is structural rather than a matter of tuning: tree-sitter's lexer is driven by parse state, so a token valid only where a command argument is expected cannot be produced on the right-hand side of an assignment, where `$a/$b` is DIVISION and already parses correctly. Widening the shared `generic_token` instead would have changed the token in every position including that one. Four forms were built and three rejected before this one, and every rejection was caught by a different gate: (1) a HIDDEN token reported 0 ERROR nodes while the tree was `command_elements: (command_argument_sep)` — the argument silently GONE, which is worse than an error because an error is visible and a missing node is not, and which the micro-repro read as `ok` until the tree was printed instead of the error count; (2) without `prec(2)` the `variable` token's `reserved` precedence won and only a PREFIX of the path was consumed, so `$a/b` appeared to work while a `..` chain did not; (3) a run whose alternation required a TRAILING separator could not match any real path, since every real path ends in a segment. The fourth form fixed a measured loss rather than a refinement: a directory argument ends in a separator — `$testDataPath\UserConfigProv\` — and without an optional trailing separator the token matched only the prefix, leaving the final `\` orphaned and costing 11 REAL cmdlet calls in one Pester file, verified by running the analyzer under both grammars (40 such calls pinned, 29 under the broken candidate) rather than inferred. Final measurement: F11 G1 damaged files 110 -> 87 with sites 755 -> 603, G2 identity 290 clean files with 0 tree differences, G3 +44 pairs against -121 — and every one of those 121 is a PATH-FRAGMENT FABRICATION: 87 name a file extension (`.txt`, `.psd1`, `.yaml`) and the rest name filename components, checked against the source (`Resolve-Path $TESTDRIVE/this.directory.is.invalid` was publishing `uses -> directory`, `uses -> is` and `uses -> invalid`). The 44 gained are real recovered calls, 18 of them `calls -> It` in Pester blocks that previously did not parse. Production corpora: 9 files fixed, 0 broken. The repro battery's named limits go 7 -> 6, and the powershell production draw's damaged files go 14 -> 10. (8) G8 is two one-character widenings, each mirroring a case the rule already had, and it is the highest-yield patch in the lane per site touched. `type_name` already recursed on `.` for a dotted type, so `+` — .NET's nested-type separator, as in `[System.Environment+SpecialFolder]` — is that same `choice` widened to a separator set, and it cannot interact with anything else because a type name's only other continuation is `.`. `command_parameter`'s class had no `=`, so `--flag=value` split at the `=` and the remainder fell to `assignement_operator`, which is not valid in command-argument position. `=` is admitted to the DOUBLE-DASH branch ONLY: a native command's `--flag=value` really is one argv token, whereas PowerShell's own parameters are `-Name value` or `-Name:value` and `-Name=value` is not valid, so widening the single-dash class would make an INVALID form parse. Measured footprints: 11 sites for the nested type and 26 for the flag, and the residue is recorded below. The yield is out of proportion to the diff because the patch makes whole regions parse. F11 G1 damaged files 87 -> 85 with ERROR LINES 8721 -> 3748, a 57% drop; G2 identity 313 clean files with 0 tree differences; G3 +608 pairs against 4 lost. The powershell production draw's damaged files go 10 -> 9 and its relationships 9,597 -> 10,111. The one symbol the gate reports as VANISHED is a promotion, and it was checked rather than argued. `build.psm1`'s `AddRemoteIfMissing` is a `param()` block parameter; parameters are carried as `parameters` METADATA on the owning function rather than as symbols, which is the lane's design and which `suppression-and-params-psb7` pins on a separate channel. Under the pinned grammar the region did not parse, so the parameter was carried NOWHERE and only the recovery reader named it, as a file-level variable. Under G8 the enclosing function parses and the parameter is carried as `Sync-PSTags -> AddRemoteIfMissing:Switch`, with its type read: 58 functions carrying 172 parameters against 57 and 171. The three remaining lost pairs (`uses -> describe` twice, `uses -> RepoRoot`) are the same recovery-fabrication class G7 removed, from a `git --git-dir=... describe` line. Residue, recorded rather than rounded off: `--flag=$var` with a VARIABLE value is still 1 MISSING, because the value after a glued `=` has no `command_argument_sep` and a bare `variable` is not among the value alternatives. That is 8 corpus sites, and PowerShell's canonical `-Name $var` is unaffected because that form does have the separator. F11 on the G5c candidate: G1 damage 137 → 135 files and MISSING 177 → 139 with 0 newly damaged, G2 identity 263 clean files with 0 tree differences, and G3 losing exactly ONE (label,target) pair — whose target F11 prints in full as a seven-line ERROR block — against +126 pairs added. That single pair is the same false-negative class as G5b's 135, and the census confirms it: NullConditional.Tests.ps1 falls 69 → 16 ERROR nodes, NativeCommandPathUpdate.Tests.ps1 goes hasError=true → false, and the three corpus files that do not use `?.` are BIT-IDENTICAL between the two grammars. (9) G9 is the last of the big classes and the only one whose DIAGNOSIS I got wrong before the measurement forced it. I recorded this class as a genuine LR ambiguity between `array_type_name` and `generic_type_name` — the two are indeed both `seq($.type_name, '[')`, identical prefixes separated only by what follows the bracket — and I expected to fix it by reprioritising. It is not an ambiguity, and the automation said so twice while I was asserting otherwise. `prec(1)` on the generic branch of `type_spec` changed nothing at all, and declaring the conflict `[$.array_type_name, $.generic_type_name]` came back `unnecessary conflicts` from `tree-sitter generate` — which is the informative part: UNNECESSARY means the automaton has no conflict there, because the generic route was never reachable. That is the third time this lane has been told 'unnecessary conflict' (G1's `param_block` and G7's hidden token are the other two) and the lesson is the same each time: it means the competing route does not EXIST, so reprioritising cannot help and the fix has to be to add the missing derivation. The real gap is one token deep: `generic_type_arguments` was `seq($.type_spec, repeat(seq(',', $.type_spec)))`, and a `type_spec` reaches the array form only as `array_type_name` = `type_name` followed by `[` — the SUFFIX. PowerShell and C# both write the PREFIX form, `[string]`, which is a `type_literal`, and no `type_spec` production can begin with a leading `[`. So `[Dictionary[[string],[int]]]` had no derivation at all; the parser took the only route available (`array_type_name` on `Dictionary[`), expected `]`, found `[`, and produced `ERROR(array_type_name(Dictionary[))` with the remainder of the line falling out as a separate expression — which is why the damage looked like an unrelated downstream error. The admitted patch widens `generic_type_arguments`' element to `choice($.type_spec, $.type_literal)`. It is additive, it needs no conflict declaration, and it is disjoint from the existing form on the FIRST TOKEN of the argument, which is the same disjointness argument that made G6 and G7 safe rather than merely lower-precedence. A process finding worth the same record as the patch, because it changed how the work was done: `tree-sitter parse` in the vendored grammar directory compiles natively and answers in about 14 SECONDS, against 19 MINUTES for the emscripten `tree-sitter build -w` that the F11 gate needs. Every A/B for this patch was taken natively first — 691 corpus files, damaged 126 -> 123, ERROR 803 -> 788, MISSING 29 -> 27, with the six control forms checked case by case — and the wasm was built once, only after the native sweep said the patch was a win. The corollary trap cost one cycle: `tree-sitter build --output x.wasm` emits an ELF shared object, not a wasm, unless `-w/--wasm` is passed, and web-tree-sitter rejects it with `need to see wasm magic number` — a `.wasm` extension is not a request for a wasm. F11 on the built candidate: G1 damaged files 85 -> 82 with sites 580 -> 560 and MISSING 85 -> 71, fixed 3, newly damaged 0, worse 0; G2 identity 315 clean files with 0 tree differences; G3 +2 pairs against 2 lost, and the verdict is INADMISSIBLE. Both 'lost' pairs are MOVES, verified from the gate's own added list rather than argued from the source, and they are a NEW instance of this lane's recurring false negative: the first three were a pair attributed to a recovery fabrication, and this one is a pair whose TARGET GOT MORE PRECISE. Generics.Tests.ps1:44 is `$x = [dictionary[[string], [int]]]::New()`; the pinned grammar could not parse the type literal, so the analyzer recovered a method named `int::New` and published `calls -> int::New`, attributing the static call to a type ARGUMENT rather than to the constructed type that is its actual receiver. Under G9 the same line publishes `calls -> dictionary[[string], [int]]::New`. Conversions.Tests.ps1:493 is `[Func[[E], [object]]] $f = $n.GetC`, and the edge moves from `uses -> object` to `uses -> Func[[E], [object]]` — from the innermost bareword to the full type reference that owns the span. Same line, same label, strictly better target, in both cases; F11 compares (label,target) as strings and so cannot tell 'more precise' from 'gone'. Production corpora: the powershell draw's damaged files go 9 -> 8 and its MISSING nodes halve, 12 -> 6, with its relationships flat at 10,111 because both moved pairs live in files outside the 49-file draw.  (10) G10 is the class the lane's own gate nearly forbade, and the reason is the most reusable finding in this record. A value GLUED to a double-dash parameter — `--git-dir="$RepoRoot/.git"`, `--flag=$var`, `--a=1` — published no edge, and the reason was that every value alternative in `_command_argument` begins with `command_argument_sep` and a glued value has none, so `redirection` won the value instead. The failure is not an error but a FABRICATION: the tree becomes a redirection carrying a MISSING `>`, which is invisible to F1, F10 and the M12 ERROR-node census, and the analyzer then publishes the value as a redirected file. Two prior measurements made it worse than invisible — on the first run of the A/B harness, which counted only ERROR, `--git-dir=$R` and `--a=1` were reported as CLEAN. Two designs were built and REJECTED before the third, and both rejections are about the LEXER rather than the parser. Attempt 1 added a `_glued_command_parameter` token requiring a trailing `=`, with `token(prec(1, ...))`, reasoning that lexical precedence would make it win exactly the ties it needed. F11 returned INADMISSIBLE: 274 clean files changed tree shape, 71 symbols changed owner, 19 pairs lost. The cause is that tree-sitter resolves LEXICAL precedence BEFORE LENGTH, so `prec(1)` made the glued token win even when its match was SHORTER — and `--flag=alnum`, which `command_parameter` matches whole and which is CLEAN across the corpus, was split into a parameter plus a value everywhere. Attempt 2 dropped the precedence, reasoning that length would then decide; that is also unworkable, because two tokens matching the SAME text at the SAME length is unresolvable by precedence OR by length, and `--a=1 --b=2` measured 2 ERROR where the pinned grammar had one SILENT MISSING. The third design has NO SECOND TOKEN. It is a PARSER alternative — `command_parameter` followed immediately by a literal or a variable, with no separator — and `command_parameter` itself is left byte-for-byte as it was, which is the entire safety argument: with nothing about the lexer moving, `--flag=alnum` cannot change shape. CORRECTION, and it is the reason this paragraph is longer than the others. The native sweep said 0 clean files changed shape, 7 became clean and 0 became broken, and the 7 was WRONG about the product. F11 runs on web-tree-sitter 0.25.9 and reported G1 fixed 0 and G3 at ZERO changed pairs: on the runtime the product actually loads, this patch is INERT. The 7 were an artefact of the native CLI being 0.26.9, and the same bytes parse differently under the two — the version skew this lane has now been bitten by repeatedly, and the first time it has bitten a patch's BENEFIT rather than its safety. What the native sweep DID establish is the half that matters for admissibility: 0 clean files changed shape, which F11 then confirmed on its own runtime at 0 differences over 318 clean files. F11 then confirmed G2 at 0 tree differences over 318 clean files and G3 at ZERO changed pairs. `generic_token` is deliberately absent from the value choice for the same reason it is absent from attempt 1: `--flag=alnum` is clean today because `command_parameter` matches the whole token, so admitting `generic_token` would split that clean node into two children. The generalisable finding is the one this lane has now paid for three times: when a construct is damaged because a TOKEN cannot reach far enough, adding a token moves the LEXER, and every clean file that relied on the old token's full extent is collateral. The fix belongs in the PARSER unless the token itself is wrong. The id digest is unchanged at 429 ids / 152 named types for exactly this reason — a parser alternative adds no node type, so no analyzer written against the old shapes is re-pointed. F11's own G1 row shows 0 fixed and G3 shows zero changed pairs. The first reading of that was a SAMPLE-CAP explanation — the gate caps at 400 files per corpus and the 7 the full sweep found are outside it. That explanation was checked and is WRONG: re-parsing the failing cases directly through web-tree-sitter 0.25.9 reproduces the errors, so the sample never saw a fix because there was none to see on this runtime. The patch is kept because it is ADMISSIBLE and free — G2 0 differences over 318 clean files, G3 zero changed pairs, id digest unchanged at 429/152 — not because it is known to help. A patch that changes nothing on the product runtime should not be described as a repair, and the grammar's own record now says so. The 38-site and 10-site corpus footprint is spent; what remains in this class is recorded below as unmeasured rather than as a plan.

alternatives.option: G5c as a new precedence level, or `?.[` for element access
alternatives.measured: REJECTED on measurement, and both halves of it came from the corpus rather than from taste. The corpus target disagrees with the documentation on the element-access form: PowerShell's own test/powershell/Language/Operators/NullConditional.Tests.ps1 uses `?[` (6 × `?[0]`, plus `?[tb]`, `?['a']`, `?[-2]`, `?[0..2]`, `?[0,1]`, `?[]`, `?[1234]`) and never `?.[`, so a `?.[` implementation would have satisfied the docs and none of the corpus. And a precedence LEVEL was rejected for the same reason G5a's named levels were: `?.` binds exactly like `.` and `?[` exactly like `[`, so the correct edit is one `choice` arm inside the rule that already defines the twin, inheriting its associativity — which is also what makes the corpus's `${psObj}?.name?.nonExistent` chain and its `(Get-Item $TestDrive)?.EnumerateFiles()?.Name` compose without a new level at all.

alternatives.option: G5 with the two precedence levels left NAMED (the first attempt)
alternatives.measured: REJECTED on measurement, and it is the most instructive rejection in this lane. It scored a clean win on every count the repro battery reports — 2 of 12 named limits fixed, 0 regressions, all 9 controls held — and the collateral gate passed too, 0 files broken. It was still the wrong patch, and only the SHAPE delta caught it: a named level emits its node in the pass-through case as well, so adding two levels wrapped EVERY expression in the language and produced 9,046 `coalesce_expression` and 9,038 `ternary_expression` nodes across 49 corpus files, re-pointing an analyzer written against the old shapes while every other number said 'pure win'. Hiding both levels makes the rules inline, so an expression using neither operator produces exactly the tree it produced before and F11's G2 identity gate passes by construction rather than by luck.

patches: use_statement / forward_statement: Sass's module system has optional clauses these rules never allowed — `as <namespace>`, `as *`, `with (<config>)`, and `show`/`hide <members>` on @forward. As written each rule was `seq('@use', $._value, ';')`, so every `as` clause was an ERROR: `@use 'sass:map';` parsed and `@use 'sass:map' as map;` — the form Sass documents — did not. Measured over 244 .scss files this was the single largest residual class, the bare token `as` at 277 error spans. Two sub-fixes were needed and the first attempt at each was wrong in an instructive way. (a) `with (<config>)` was first written to allow only `$._value`, so `with ($a: 1)` matched the `$a` and then reported `(UNEXPECTED '1')` — which reads like a value problem and is actually a missing `:` separator, because Sass's clause is a list of `$name: value` PAIRS. (b) the `as` clause was first written with `$._value`, which admits `binary_expression` and collided with the dashed-prefix form. The `as` target is therefore `choice($.identifier, $.variable, $._concatenated_identifier)`, and the whole clause is modelled in the grammar's OWN loose style (the `$._value, repeat(seq(optional(','), $._value))` pattern already at lines 86-87) rather than with a strict grammar for Sass config objects: a strict model is a second research project, and the analyzer reads these clauses by SLICING node.text, never by naming a node type, because slicing text cannot fall behind a grammar change (M60 R10). Repro: @use 'sass:map' as map;

declaration + parameter: Sass's `!default` / `!global` flag. The declaration rule allowed `optional($.important)` and nothing else, so `$a: 1 !default;` — the most common line in a Sass variable file, and the entire point of a configurable default — was an ERROR, at 210 occurrences across the corpus. Applied at BOTH sites: a variable declaration and a mixin/function parameter default, which is where Sass puts it most often (`@mixin button($bg: $grey !default)`). Repro: $x: 1 !default;

list_value + parenthesized_value (LOCAL PATCH 4): MAP LITERALS. `map.merge((...), $default)` did not parse in ANY form -- measured over 12 hand-built cases, every map form failed (single pair, several pairs, trailing comma, `$var` key, `$var` value, bare-identifier key, multi-line, nested) while lists passed, so the rule was the whole of the gap. Patched by EXTENDING TWO EXISTING RULES rather than adding a third, which is the entire content of the patch: `list_value` also accepts a keyed entry `KEY ':' VALUE`, and the inherited CSS `parenthesized_value` is widened from `'(' $._value ')'` to also accept `'(' $._value ':' $._value ')'`. The single-pair form is why it looked arbitrary -- it lost to `parenthesized_value` while two-or-more pairs parsed, because a comma settles the conflict before precedence is consulted, and `prec.dynamic` cannot help because the conflict is resolved when the parser is GENERATED. Three EARLIER attempts at this same gap added a new `map_value` rule and were measured and REVERTED (SCSS-L8): in `_value` at prec 1 it fixed 5 files and regressed none while driving ERROR nodes 3,900 -> 8,056; scoped to call arguments it fixed 4 and REGRESSED 9; with `prec.dynamic` it was worse. A new rule competes in every declaration, selector and interpolation in the language, and where it loses tree-sitter recovers with an error node -- which is why the file-level A/B reported '0 regressed' on a change that made the lane's worst files much worse. Adding no new rule is what makes this one clean: +7 files, 0 regressed, ERROR 3,900 -> 3,340. Measured: 10 of the 12 cases now parse, including the `map.merge` shape the corpus actually uses.

_include_arguments (LOCAL PATCH 5): the `@include` CLOSING delimiter no longer demands immediacy. The rule used `token.immediate` on BOTH parens, and `token.immediate` means zero intervening whitespace, so an `@include` whose argument list was not written with the parens hard against the argument did not parse at all -- `@include f( 1px );` fails on a single SPACE on one line, and the multi-line form (a design-system stylesheet's house style) fails too. A plain call with the same layout always parsed, which localises the fault to this rule's delimiters rather than to Sass or the lexer. It is the FIRST error in 15 of the 63 element-plus files that still failed, across `set-css-var-value` (10) and `css-var-from-global` (5). Only the closing delimiter is relaxed; `token.immediate('(')` stays because Sass genuinely forbids whitespace between a mixin name and its argument list. Measured: +8 files, 0 regressed, ERROR 3,340 -> 3,089.

DECLARED, NOT PATCHED: `@forward 'x' as prefix-*;`, the PREFIX form of the `as` clause. It requires `repeat1(seq('-', …))` after the name, which tree-sitter reports as an unresolved conflict with `binary_expression` (a `$._value` can itself be `a - b`). It occurs ZERO times in 40,521 lines of corpus, where 359 uses are `as *` and 1 is `as common`. The A/B carries it as `forward-as-dashed-prefix` with verdict `unchanged-broken` rather than omitting it, so the unsupported form is named in the evidence instead of absent from it. A grammar conflict taken on for a construct with no evidence is a risk incurred on somebody else's behalf.

The alternative was to leave .scss on the CSS grammar, which is where it was routed: 43 of 244 files parsed clean (17.6%) with 30,767 ERROR nodes, because the CSS grammar has no `$variables`, no `@mixin`/`@include`, no `@use`/`@forward` and no interpolation. That is a real project with a real risk of silent shape change, and it was declined in favour of two measured patches.
